messages.subject: State-space model?
parts:
Hi, I am trying to fit a state space model using Nimble.

But, I am not sure what is wrong. I followed the steps shown in this example https://nature.berkeley.edu/~pdevalpine/nimbleExamples/particle_filter/pfExample.html


Here is the model. T1 and T2 are latent states. Te, Ti, and q are observed data. deltaT is constant. C1, C2, R1, R2, and R3 are parameters.  sigma1,2,3 are gaussian noise with mean 0.


I recovered my code and data below. In the example, we didn't initialize x (latent state). And there is one state. But, my case, I got errors if I didn';t initialize it. Also, I have two states (T1 and T2).

I tried to put T1 and T2 together in a matrix, but it didn't work.

Can you give  me any suggestions?


Thank you so much..!!


library(nimble)



rm(list=ls())

X <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ecosang/tt/master/bldg1_dat.csv", sep=";", header=FALSE)

## Set the names of the columns in X

names(X) <- c("t","Te","Ti","q")


set.seed(1)

dim(X$Te)

## define the model

stateSpaceCode <- nimbleCode({

  C1 ~ T(dnorm(100, 5),90,100)

  C2 ~ T(dnorm(50, 5),40,50)

  R1 ~ T(dnorm(1, 0.5),0.001,2)

  R2 ~ T(dnorm(2, 1),0.001,4)

  R3 ~ T(dnorm(0.5, 0.25),0.001,1)

  sigma1~dunif(1e-03,2)

  sigma2~dunif(1e-03,2)

  sigma3~dunif(1e-03,2)

  T1[1] ~ dnorm(8,sigma1)

  T2[1] ~ dnorm(12,sigma2)

  for (t in 1:(TT-1)){




    T1[t+1]~dnorm(mean=( T1[t]+((T2[t]-T1[t])/(C1*R2)+(Te[t]-T1[t])/(C1*R1))*dt  ),sd=sigma1)

    T2[t+1]~dnorm(mean=( T2[t]+((Ti[t]-T2[t])/(C2*R3)+(T1[t]-T2[t])/(C2*R2))*dt  ),sd=sigma2)

    q[t]~dnorm(mean=(Ti[t]-T2[t])/R3,sd=sigma3)

  }

  q[TT]~dnorm(mean=(Ti[TT]-T2[TT])/R3,sd=sigma3)




})  




## define data, constants, and initial values  

dat <- list(q=X$q,Ti=X$Ti,Te=X$Te[-length(X$Te)]) #X$Te




constants <- list(

    dt = 1,

    TT=(dim(X)[1])

)




inits <- list(

  C1=100,

  C2=50,

  R1=1,

  R2=2,

  R3=0.5,

  sigma1=0.5,

  sigma2=0.5,

  sigma3=0.5,

  T1=rep(8,(dim(X)[1])),

  T2=rep(12,(dim(X)[1]))

)




## build the model

stateSpaceModel <- nimbleModel(stateSpaceCode,

                              data = dat,

                              constants = constants,

                              init=inits,

                              check = FALSE)




## create MCMC specification for the state space model

stateSpaceMCMCconf <- configureMCMC(stateSpaceModel, nodes = NULL)




## add a block pMCMC sampler for a, b, sigPN, and sigOE

stateSpaceMCMCconf$addSampler(target = c('C1', 'C2','R1', 'R2','R3', 'sigma1', 'sigma2', 'sigma3'),

                              type = 'RW_PF_block', control = list(latents = c('T1','T2')))










stateSpaceMCMC <- buildMCMC(stateSpaceMCMCconf)

compiledList <- compileNimble(stateSpaceModel, stateSpaceMCMC, resetFunctions = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: State-space model?
parts: Thanks for asking and for including an example of your error!  One current limitation of NIMBLE's particle filtering methods (as I think you realized) is that all of the latent states have to be held in the same variable.  This should be fixed in  a future version of NIMBLE, but for now you will have to model your two latent state variables (T1 and T2) as a single matrix.  I rewrote your model slightly to accomplish this, turning T1 and T2 into a single matrix T_12, where T_12[1, t] corresponds to T1[t] and T_12[2, t] corresponds to T2[t].

stateSpaceCode <- nimbleCode({
  
  C1 ~ T(dnorm(100, 5),90,100)
  
  C2 ~ T(dnorm(50, 5),40,50)
  
  R1 ~ T(dnorm(1, 0.5),0.001,2)
  
  R2 ~ T(dnorm(2, 1),0.001,4)
  
  R3 ~ T(dnorm(0.5, 0.25),0.001,1)
  
  sigma1~dunif(1e-03,2)
  
  sigma2~dunif(1e-03,2)
  
  sigma3~dunif(1e-03,2)

T_12[1, t+1]~dnorm(mean=( T_12[1, t]+((T_12[2, t]-T_12[1, t])/(C1*R2)+(Te[t]-T_12[1, t])/(C1*R1))*dt  ),sd=sigma1)
    
    T_12[2, t+1]~dnorm(mean=( T_12[2, t]+((Ti[t]-T_12[2, t])/(C2*R3)+(T_12[1, t]-T_12[2, t])/(C2*R2))*dt  ),sd=sigma2)
    
    q[t]~dnorm(mean=(Ti[t]-T_12[2, t])/R3,sd=sigma3)
    
  }
  
  q[TT]~dnorm(mean=(Ti[TT]-T_12[2, TT])/R3,sd=sigma3)
  
}) 

I also changed the initial values, so that T_12 was given a matrix of initial values, and updated the "latents" control list argument for the "RW_PF_block" sampler to be "T_12" instead of "c(T1, T2)".  After this, the particle MCMC algorithm was able to compile and run successfully.  Let me know if you try this out and it doesn't work though, or if you have any other questions.  Thanks again!
